title: Weighted benchmark harness for multitask calibrated quantization
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a reusable benchmark harness that computes a single weighted quality index across heterogeneous tasks (perplexity, MMLU-style multi-choice accuracy, Rouge/BLEU for summarization/translation, and task-specific scorers for QA/code). The harness will run calibration and validation sweeps for FP8 and INT8 quant profiles, produce per-task and aggregated reports, and emit gating signals for rollout decisions. This ticket implements the orchestrator, metric adapters, and reporting glue; model execution and kernel-level optimizations are handled in separate runtime tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute a defined task matrix (language modeling, closed-book QA, summarization, translation, code synthesis) against both FP8 and INT8 quant profiles and record metrics for each run.
Metrics include: perplexity (where applicable), MMLU-style accuracy/top-k accuracy, Rouge-1/2/L/F1, BLEU, and at least two task-specific scorers (QA F1/em, code exact match and relative pass@k).

Output is a single JSON report with per-task metrics, normalized scores, and a weighted aggregate score calculable from a profile file. Report schema documented in Confluence and compatible with the existing quality dashboard.
Calibration sweep runner supports: calibration dataset selection, histogram/activation collectors, per-layer scale reconciliation, and can be throttled to match Dedicated capacity windows.
A gating rule prototype consumes the aggregate score and signals PASS/WARN/FAIL with clear thresholds and confidence intervals (bootstrap-based).
Integration tests that run a tiny end-to-end flow on a small test model (CPU/GPU) and assert report schema + reasonable metric ranges.
implementation_notes: Design a metric adapter interface: accepts raw model outputs + task metadata, returns canonical metric entries (name, value, n_samples, seed).
Normalize generation metrics by task difficulty: implement per-task reference baselines and an easy-to-configure weighting file stored in S3/Drive.
Perplexity: compute both token-level and sequence-level perplexities; report geometric mean and effective-entropy-adjusted scores.
MMLU-style: support prompt templates + multiple choice evaluation harness; handle logits-to-prob conversions consistently across quantized kernels.
Rouge/BLEU: use stable tokenization pipeline (shared with console/analytics) and include deterministic sampling for stochastic decoders during calibration runs.

Task-specific scorers: integrate squad-style EM/F1 for extractive QA, chrF for translation sanity checks, and a lightweight test harness to run code execution in sandboxed containers for pass@k metrics.

Calibration workflow: orchestration step defines calibration dataset slices, runs short calibration jobs per-profile, collects activation statistics, and stores calibration artifacts under /calibrations/{model}/{profile}/{timestamp}.
Statistical gating: compute 95% confidence intervals via bootstrap for the aggregate score, and require delta > configured minimum lift before PASS for new quant profile vs baseline.
Reporting: produce both human-readable HTML summary (for reviewers) and machine-readable JSON for dashboards and automated rollouts.
Performance: add lightweight sampling mode for smoke runs to reduce cost during developer iteration; full-sweep runs reserved for CI and nightly builds.
test_plan: Unit tests for each metric adapter with synthetic predictions and edge cases (all OOV tokens, identical predictions, empty outputs).
Integration test: small end-to-end run with tiny-lm (1M params) quantized to INT8 and FP8 using the harness; assert schema + plausible deltas relative to float baseline.
CI job that runs harness in 'sample' mode on PRs changed under /metrics or /calibration, and nightly full-run on main branch across 3 representative models.
A/B plot generation that shows per-task contributions to the weighted score and the raw distributions for manual review.
risks: Metric mismatches due to tokenizer drift between evaluation harness and upstream production tokenization — mitigate by pinning tokenizer version and including tokenizer hash in reports.
Calibration artifacts may not transfer between hardware vendors (kernel numeric differences) — add hardware tags and include cross-hardware comparisons in reports.
High cost of full-sweep runs if not throttled — require quota checks and sample mode defaults for non-nightly runs.
Ambiguity in task weighting could produce unintuitive aggregate scores; include reviewer tooling and store historic weighting changes for audits.
dependencies_notes: Relies on existing quant profile outputs from ENG-4219 for profile metadata formats.
Uses eval harness adapters planned in ENG-6241 and dataset splits from ENG-2384.
UI/Console ingestion expects the report schema agreed with console team (separate sync required).
